thread:
Sasha (Product): Quick sync — we have three customer asks (Acme, Beacon, Orion) that overlap on private deployment + dedicated capacity + stricter KMS requirements. I want to consolidate into one prioritized deliverable for Q3. Who blocks what and what are realistic gating criteria?

Luca (Product): Thanks. My proposal: 1) MVP private deploy (no HSM) + Reserved Dedicated path; 2) Post-MVP add HSM/KMS for Acme. That way we can unblock Beacon and Orion earlier. Thoughts?

Kevin (Eng/runtime): Feasibility: runtime can support a private control plane + dedicated pools, but we need ~6 weeks to validate large-sequence perf (prefix caching + batching) and another 2 weeks for canary rollout tooling. Main risk is memory fragmentation with current quantized kernels under high concurrency.

Maya (Eng/infra): Capacity note: Dedicated pools require GPU procurement if >2x baseline. We can shim with burst on hosted for 6-8 weeks but SLA drops. Also need network route approvals for VPC peering (security review) — that adds ~1 week to schedule.

Arzoo (Security): For Acme's HSM requirement: we need an audit and threat model plus HSM integration tests. That’s usually a 3-week dependency after infra allocates staging. If we split HSM to post-MVP as Luca suggested, we can avoid blocking the whole deliverable. Also need to confirm acceptable in-transit encryption and KMS rotation policy.

Kevin (Eng/runtime): To be concrete: runtime tasks = perf validation (6w), canary infra + fallback policy (1w), rollback automation (1w). If product is okay with a reduced token-limit for MVP (e.g., 2k vs 8k), we can shave 2 weeks off perf validation.

Sasha (Product): Good — tradeoff looks reasonable. Can you write a minimal perf acceptance criteria? e.g., p95 latency <= 200ms for short seq, fallbacks on overload, and memory < 75% under 80% concurrency. I can align customers to the token-limit trade.

Kevin (Eng/runtime): Draft acceptance checklist:
- p95 latency (seq <=512) <= 200ms
- graceful fallback to cheaper model variant when queueing > 200ms
- KV cache hit-rate >= 30% on repeated prefixes
- memory usage ceiling < 75% under 80% concurrency
- end-to-end warm startup < 15s
(we can put this in the canary runbook)

Maya (Eng/infra): Infra checklist / gating:
- VPC peering and route tables approved
- Dedicated pool slot reservation confirmed (or burst fallback plan)
- Monitoring: token-level billing + latency traces enabled
- Autoscale policy: min 2 nodes, max 10 nodes (we can adjust)
- Staging infra with HSM creds (if HSM path chosen)

Arzoo (Security): Security gating:
- Threat model for private control plane signed off
- KMS integration test matrix passing
- Audit logging & access review completed
- HSM acceptance tests (post-MVP for Acme)

Luca (Product): Proposed launch criteria (MVP):
- Runtime perf checklist all green at canary
- Infra staging + peering validated
- Security threat model + baseline KMS pass
- Customer acceptance test with Beacon (pilot)
If all green, soft-launch to Orion and Beacon, Acme on opt-in for HSM post-MVP.

Sasha (Product): Ok — next steps: 1) Kevin write perf acceptance doc and link runbook; 2) Maya create infra ticket with ETA and burst plan; 3) Arzoo draft threat model checklist; 4) Luca coordinate customer pilot for Beacon. Can we aim for initial canary in 7 weeks?

Kevin (Eng/runtime): I can get the perf doc + runbook in 3 business days. Canary in 7 weeks is tight but doable if product confirms token-limit trade now.

Maya (Eng/infra): I'll file infra ticket and note procurement window. If procurement hits, we'll use burst fallback — I'll attach cost delta.

Arzoo (Security): I'll start the threat model and post the checklist in #eng-security for review by EOD Thursday.

deploy-bot: canary-deploy queued for 2835100000 (staging) :rocket:

Sasha (Product): Great — I'll update customers and confirm the token-limit trade by EOD tomorrow. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
